rows.jp: 教室に戻る途中、処女がうずくまっていた。
rows.en: On my way back to the classroom, I found a virgin crouched in the hall.

ghs.en: I met a crouching maiden while on my way back to the classroom.
ghs.assessment: 処女 explicitly means 'virgin' and is the narrator's deliberately inappropriate label. 'Maiden' euphemizes and changes that pointed diction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'On my way back to class, I found a virgin crouched in the hall.'

highlights.text: I met a crouching maiden while on my way back to the classroom.

ghs.assessment: Sudden versus swift is a small manner distinction rather than a changed event.
ghs.remedy: Use sudden if the onset matters.

highlights.text: Very sudden behavior.

rows.jp: ゆっくりと振り返った。

rows.en: She looked up and gave me a little nod.

ghs.en: She raises her head and nods in salutation.

rows.jp: いつもと変わる風でもない美希だ。
rows.en: Miki seemed exactly the same as ever.

ghs.en: Miki's style is an ever unchanging, bluff-less thing.
ghs.assessment: Ever unchanging preserves same as usual; bluff-less style is unsupported and incoherent.
ghs.remedy: Say simply that she seemed the same as ever.

highlights.text: Miki's style is an ever unchanging, bluff-less thing.

ghs.en: A vague sense of physical discomfort.
ghs.assessment: 違和感 is a sense that something is off or incongruous. 'Physical discomfort' incorrectly makes it a bodily symptom.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Still, something feels slightly off.'

highlights.text: A vague sense of physical discomfort.

rows.jp: 美希は、こんな強かったのだろうか？
rows.en: Had Miki always been this strong?

ghs.en: Was Miki always this determined and strong?

rows.jp: もともと素質はあったようだが、一回りも二回りもたくましくなったような。
rows.en: She had always shown promise, but now she seemed a whole lot tougher.

ghs.en: That quality was there from the start, yes, but it feels she has gone around the block once or twice with regards to strength of willpower.
ghs.assessment: The prior quality and increased strength survive, but gone around the block imports an experience idiom and narrows the growth to willpower.
ghs.remedy: Preserve the one-or-two-level increase in toughness.

highlights.text: That quality was there from the start, yes, but it feels she has gone around the block once or twice with regards to strength of willpower.

rows.en: That was the impression I got.

rows.jp: 「表面的な言葉遊びで送辞と相似とか言いますか？」
rows.en: “Are you about to make some shallow joke about mopping and moping?”

ghs.en: Miki: "Is that a superficial wordplay with your idea of my physical characteristics and your parentage?"

ghs.assessment: The reply denies an intended future move, 'I wasn't going to.' 'It is not' has neither the correct subject nor the intended temporal relation.
ghs.remedy: Use '...I wasn't going to!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "...it is not!"

rows.jp: 「そんなオチを封じた上にせかすなようっっ」
rows.en: “Don’t steal my punch line and then rush meee!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Don't hurry me with that when I don't have a comebaaack!"

ghs.assessment: The stronger judgment survives, but the English is verbless and narrows general toughness to willpower.
ghs.remedy: Use a finite clause describing increased toughness.

highlights.text: Stronger willpower.

ghs.en: Miki: "Then you're the culprit you bastaaard!"

rows.jp: 胴体に一発当たってしまった。
rows.en: One of her blows caught me square in the body.

ghs.en: Smacked with one blow to the torso.

ghs.assessment: The English changes the question's shape and adds causal how, but surprise at her strength survives.
ghs.remedy: Keep the compact surprised question.

highlights.text: Ugh, so strong, but how?

rows.jp: カラデをおさめたこの俺を。

ghs.en: To hit I, the Master of Karade!
ghs.assessment: Being struck and Master of Karade are recoverable. The defect is broken case and grammar.
ghs.remedy: Use grammatical mock-indignant English.

highlights.text: To hit I, the Master of Karade!

rows.jp: ちょっぴり本気になる。

ghs.en: It got just a smidgen serious.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says the narrator gets a little serious. 'It got ... serious' removes the acting subject and turns his decision into a change in the situation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I get just a little serious.'

highlights.text: It got just a smidgen serious.

rows.jp: しなやかな脚が、腰より高くあがった。
rows.en: One supple leg swept higher than her waist.

ghs.en: A flexible leg rose higher than her hips.

rows.jp: 軸足を払ってやろうと思ったが、白パンツが垣間見えた。
rows.en: I was about to take out her standing leg when I caught a glimpse of white panties.

ghs.en: I was thinking how to sweep off the leg she uses as axle, but through the gap, I saw panties.
ghs.assessment: 軸足 is the planted or pivot leg, not an 'axle' leg, and 白 explicitly says the briefly seen panties are white. The English both calques the martial term and omits the color.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I consider sweeping her planted leg, but catch a glimpse of white panties.'

highlights.text: I was thinking how to sweep off the leg she uses as axle, but through the gap, I saw panties.

ghs.assessment: Attack suspension is bureaucratic but still communicates that the attack is called off.
ghs.remedy: Use a natural command to call off the attack.

highlights.text: Attack suspension.

rows.jp: 男太一、眼前に供えられたパンツを見ないなどという惰弱な選択肢はない。
rows.en: Taichi, Man Among Men, could never choose the coward’s path of ignoring the panties laid before him.

ghs.en: To Taichi the Man not looking at panties sacrificed to his sight is an effeminate choice that does not exists.
ghs.assessment: 惰弱 means cowardly or feeble, not specifically effeminate, and 'does not exists' is ungrammatical. The sentence's mock-heroic self-designation is also left syntactically stranded.
ghs.remedy: Use 'For Taichi the Man, cowardly refusal to look at panties offered before his eyes is no option at all.'

highlights.text: To Taichi the Man not looking at panties sacrificed to his sight is an effeminate choice that does not exists.

rows.jp: 腰を落として視線を下げた。
rows.en: I dropped my stance and lowered my eyes.

ghs.en: I dropped my gaze to below the hips.
ghs.assessment: The narrator lowers his stance and then lowers his gaze. 'I dropped my gaze to below the hips' omits the bodily movement and invents a spatial object for the gaze.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I lower my stance and drop my gaze.'

highlights.text: I dropped my gaze to below the hips.

rows.jp: カラデによる中段受けにて備える。
rows.en: I raised a karade middle block.

ghs.en: As per Karade, I steady myself to take it in the mid-section.
ghs.assessment: 中段受け is a middle-level block. The English says he prepares to take the kick in his midsection, reversing defense into receiving the blow.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I brace with a Karade middle-level block.'

highlights.text: As per Karade, I steady myself to take it in the mid-section.

rows.jp: 腕の間を、つまさきは柔らかく貫通してきた。
rows.en: Her toes slipped softly between my arms and pierced my guard.

ghs.en: In the space between the arms, the tip of the toes softly breaches through.

ghs.assessment: The only confirmed defect is a missing opening quotation mark.
ghs.remedy: Restore the opening quotation mark.

highlights.text: Taichi: Huh?"

rows.jp: 「あ、よかった。気がつきましたか？」

ghs.en: Miki: "Ah, I'm so glad! Did you recover now?"
ghs.assessment: The immediate waking context makes regained consciousness clear, despite the broad and awkward recover wording.
ghs.remedy: Ask naturally whether she is awake or has come to.

highlights.text: Miki: "Ah, I'm so glad! Did you recover now?"

rows.jp: 「う、うー。俺ってばどれくらい気絶してた？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Uh, ugggh... how long have I been out?"

rows.jp: 「あー、ついに美希に負けたかー！」
rows.en: “Ah, so the day has finally come! I’ve lost to Miki!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Awww, and in the end Miki beat meee!"

ghs.assessment: 膝を打つ here is to slap one's knee. 'Pound my lap' names a different body area and a more violent action.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I slap my knee.'

highlights.text: I pound my lap.

rows.jp: 「でもすごく油断してらしたじゃないですか」
rows.en: “You did let your guard down pretty badly.”

ghs.en: Miki: "But you were really off-guard, weren't you?"

rows.jp: 「いやー、あれは俺にとって他に選択肢がないからなー」
rows.en: “Well, I didn’t exactly have another option.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Naaah, it was because there were no other choices for me..."

rows.jp: 「……たぶん命がかかっていても同じだった」
rows.en: “...I’d probably have done the same with my life on the line.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...perhaps, even if my life was at stake, that wouldn't have changed."

rows.en: I wagged a finger at her.

ghs.en: I show her a wiggling finger.

rows.jp: 「ライブで見る素人娘がリアルに着用しているパンツ、だよ、君」
rows.en: “Panties worn by a real amateur girl, live and in person, my dear.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "For the live show of 'serious' panties worn by an amateur girl, that's what!"
ghs.assessment: リアル modifies the fact that the underwear is really being worn and viewed live. The English turns it into 'serious panties,' which has no support in the Japanese.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Panties actually being worn by an amateur girl you're watching live, my boy.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "For the live show of 'serious' panties worn by an amateur girl, that's what!"

rows.en: “All the difference in the world. Like so—”

ghs.assessment: 違うとも emphatically agrees that the proposed equivalence is different before demonstrating how. 'So true' reverses that reply into a denial of Miki's objection.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Different indeed. Like this—'

highlights.text: Taichi: "So true. Like THIS!---"

rows.jp: 愛弟子の短いスカートのはしをつまんだ愛指が。
rows.en: My favorite fingers pinched the hem of my favorite apprentice’s short skirt.

ghs.en: Loving fingers pinch the hem of my loved pupil's short skirt.

rows.jp: チョキで、しっかと挟まれているっ！
rows.en: And she caught them firmly between two scissoring fingers!

ghs.en: And a scissor of fingers cleanly pushes them away!
ghs.assessment: The source says the skirt hem is firmly caught between a scissors-shaped pair of fingers. 'A scissor of fingers ... pushes them away' changes both the grip and its direction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Only to be caught fast between two fingers held like scissors!'

highlights.text: And a scissor of fingers cleanly pushes them away!

rows.jp: 横たわって膝を抱え、エビチリみたいに丸くなった。
rows.en: I lay down, hugged my knees, and curled up like a shrimp in chili sauce.

ghs.en: I grab back my stretched-out knees, and hug them until I look as round as a fried shrimp.
ghs.assessment: エビチリ is chili shrimp, not fried shrimp, and the narrator lies down and curls up while hugging his knees. 'Grab back my stretched-out knees' does not describe that posture.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I lie down, hug my knees, and curl up like a chili shrimp.'

highlights.text: I grab back my stretched-out knees, and hug them until I look as round as a fried shrimp.

ghs.en: Taichi: "Then it's an oily good time for me to retire."

rows.jp: ゆさゆさと揺すられる。
rows.en: Miki rocked me back and forth.

ghs.en: I was shaken and quaked like a certain too yu-ng girl.

rows.jp: 「ししょー、元気出してくださいよ」

ghs.assessment: Shishou is foreignization or romanization, not semantic mistranslation.
ghs.remedy: Use the established English title.

highlights.text: Miki: "Shishou, please stay strong!"

rows.jp: 「またはじまったよこの人は」

ghs.en: Miki: "He's started it again, this guy..."

rows.jp: フランス人のように問い返す。

ghs.en: I return that question like a Frenchman.
Miki: "When it's all normal with everyone."

rows.en: All at once, her voice began to tremble.

rows.jp: 「ほら、こんなに手が震えてます」
rows.en: “Look. My hands are shaking this badly.”

ghs.en: Miki: "Look, my hands are shaking this much."

rows.jp: 広げた両手が、汗ばんで、かじかむように。
rows.en: She held both hands out to me, clammy and cramped as if from cold.

ghs.en: She opens out her hands, and they are sweaty as if numb with cold.

rows.jp: まるで怯えているかの如く。

ghs.en: Exactly as if she had become frightened.

rows.jp: 「それはもう、せんぱいのプレッシャーみたいっぽいやつに当てられて、小心者の美希はビビリまくりなわけですよ」
rows.en: “You’ve got this, like, pressure-ish thing coming off you, and timid little Miki is scared out of her wits.”

ghs.en: Miki: "That's because, when affected by Senpai's straining at the mental pressure, cowardly little Miki just jumps all into the jitter-jitters."
ghs.assessment: The source says Miki is being overwhelmed by something like pressure emanating from Senpai. 'Senpai's straining at the mental pressure' makes him the person under strain and misassigns the relation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Something like your pressure is getting to timid little Miki, so she's scared stiff.'

highlights.text: Miki: "That's because, when affected by Senpai's straining at the mental pressure, cowardly little Miki just jumps all into the jitter-jitters."

rows.jp: 「だから、元気出してください」
励ましてくれているだろうか。
rows.en: Was she trying to encourage me?

rows.jp: 様子が変なのが気になるけど。
rows.en: Her strange behavior bothered me, though.

ghs.en: I do worry as things are a bit odd, though.

rows.jp: うーむ、ポワワとしてしまうではないか。
rows.en: Still, she was making me feel all warm and fuzzy.

ghs.en: Ye-ep, let's just puff those cheeks and give a good smile, won't we.
ghs.assessment: ポワワ describes the narrator going soft, dreamy, or warmly fuzzy in response. Puffing cheeks and deliberately producing a smile are actions invented by the English.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Hmm. She's making me go all soft and fuzzy.'

highlights.text: Ye-ep, let's just puff those cheeks and give a good smile, won't we.

rows.jp: 「よし、免許皆伝をやろうではないか」
rows.en: “Very well. I shall award you your master’s license.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well, how about we formalize this mastery of yours?"

rows.en: I punched one fist into my palm.

ghs.en: I make a fist as if throwing rock.
ghs.assessment: The English adds rock-paper-scissors imagery to the compact fist gesture, but the underlying gesture remains.
ghs.remedy: Describe the fist gesture without the unsupported analogy.

highlights.text: I make a fist as if throwing rock.

ghs.en: Miki: "Really been a long while there."

rows.jp: なんとも切なそうな顔をする。
rows.en: Her expression was almost unbearably wistful.

ghs.en: She makes a face that looks very pained.

rows.jp: というか（というか？）泣きそう（泣きそう？）ではないか。
rows.en: Or rather (or rather?), she looked ready to cry (did she?).

ghs.en: Or should I say (should I say?), isn't she as if about to cry (about to cry?).

rows.jp: 多重に思ってしまったぞ。
rows.en: I managed to second-guess myself twice in one sentence.

ghs.en: I thought that in a parallel multiplex didn't I.

rows.jp: 美希はメイトブックを取り出す。
rows.en: Miki took out her Mate Book.

rows.jp: 当校では身分証明書をかねるこの手帳を、『都会』の駅裏にある人気ＮＯ１高級浴場『メイトブック』にちなんでそう呼ぶ。
rows.en: At our school, the Mate Book doubled as a student ID. We called it that after the number-one luxury bathhouse behind the station in the ‘Big City.’

ghs.en: So is called this intra-school ID booklet with a second role, named after the high-class bathhouse #1 in popularity located in the popular spot behind the main City's train station, MateBook.
ghs.assessment: The source explains that the handbook doubles as school ID and is jokingly named after a popular high-end bathhouse behind the station in the City. The English's clause structure is ungrammatical and invents an additional 'popular spot.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'At our school, this handbook doubles as ID; we call it the Matebook after the number-one luxury bathhouse behind the station in the City.'

highlights.text: So is called this intra-school ID booklet with a second role, named after the high-class bathhouse #1 in popularity located in the popular spot behind the main City's train station, MateBook.

rows.jp: ちなんでねぇよ、と自らに突っ込む。
rows.en: No, we didn’t, I shot back at myself.

ghs.en: Named after my ass!, I straight-man myself.

rows.en: The matching names were pure coincidence.

ghs.en: In truth it's just a coincidence.

ghs.assessment: Sob describes rather than performs the sniffing sound. This is a presentation distinction, not a lost event.
ghs.remedy: Use an acoustic sob or sniff cue.

highlights.text: Miki: "...sob."

rows.jp: というか（というか？）泣いてる（泣いてる？）。
rows.en: Or rather (or rather?), she was crying (was she?).

ghs.en: Or should I say (or should I say?), she's crying (she's crying?).

rows.jp: 多重に思ってしまったぞ。
rows.en: I managed to second-guess myself twice in one sentence.

ghs.en: I thought that in a parallel multiplex didn't I.

rows.jp: 「……やっぱり、けっこうショックだったのかな？」
rows.en: “...Was it that much of a shock after all?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...as I thought, that was something quite shocking wasn't it?"

rows.jp: 「こんなことになって、世界が」

ghs.en: Taichi: "That the world would end up like this."

ghs.assessment: ため here is a pause or hesitation in the response. 'A subtle effect' selects an unrelated sense and removes the conversational timing.
ghs.remedy: Use 'There is a slight pause.'

highlights.text: There was a subtle effect.

ghs.en: Miki: "So it did, so it seems."
ghs.assessment: そうですね、そうかも means 'Yes, maybe so.' 'So it did, so it seems' invents a completed event and does not express tentative agreement.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Yes... maybe so.'

highlights.text: Miki: "So it did, so it seems."

rows.jp: 「俺だってびっくりだ。こんなの」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Gave me a scare too, this stuff."

rows.jp: 「もう１３歳とか１５歳の新じゃがならぬ新処女と出会う機会はなくなったわけだよなぁ」
rows.en: “So I’ll never again meet a fresh crop of thirteen- or fifteen-year-old potatoes—no, virgins.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Now, all opportunities to meet Unnew Potatoes New Virgins of 13 or 15 years of age are all gone."

ghs.assessment: そっちかい is a sharp comic rebuke meaning 'That's what you care about?!' 'That's the point then' flattens both the challenge and its target.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That's what you're upset about?!'

highlights.text: Miki: "That's the point then."

rows.jp: 「美希は手帳だいぶ使いこんでるなあ。ぼろぼろだ」
rows.en: “You’ve really put this Mate Book through its paces, Miki. It’s falling apart.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You've been using this notebook thoroughly, Miki. It's all worn!"

rows.jp: 無意味に繰り返すことで肯定する美希。
rows.en: Miki confirmed it by pointlessly repeating me.

ghs.en: Miki assents by meaninglessly repeating my words.

rows.jp: ページを繰ると、メモ欄にはすでに俺のサインがでかでかと書かれていた。
rows.en: I flipped through the pages and found my enormous signature already scrawled across the notes section.

ghs.en: Flipping the pages, I see annotation fields filled with my large-sized signature.

rows.jp: 何ページにも渡っている。

ghs.assessment: 何ページにも渡っている says the signature exercise extends across many pages. 'I pass by several pages' makes the narrator the subject of an unrelated action.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It goes on for pages.'

highlights.text: I pass by several pages.

rows.jp: 俺様サイン練習帳といった有様になっている。
rows.en: It had practically become a practice book for the Great Taichi’s autograph.

ghs.en: This is beginning to look like a practice notebook for my signatures.

rows.jp: 白紙を見つけ、そこに新たなサインを書き込む。
rows.en: I found a blank spot and added a new one.

ghs.en: I find a blank page and there I fill out a fresh signature.

rows.jp: いつ頃からかはじまった、俺たちのお遊びだ。
rows.en: It was a silly little game we had started who knew when.

ghs.en: How long ago it was when we began to play?
ghs.assessment: The source calls this a harmless game of theirs that began at some point. The English turns it into a question about elapsed time and omits the game.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It's a little game of ours that started somewhere along the way.'

highlights.text: How long ago it was when we began to play?

rows.jp: 受け取って、美希は胸元に抱える。
rows.en: Miki took it and held it against her chest.

ghs.en: Miki takes it, and hugs it to her chest,

rows.jp: 失われた日常を、かき抱くように。
rows.en: As though she were clutching our lost everyday life to her chest.

ghs.en: As if holding the very ordinary days now lost.

rows.jp: ちょっとあふれた涙を、ぬぐってやりもする。
rows.en: I even wiped away the little tear that escaped.

ghs.en: Copying that, I go and wipe those tears now overflowing.
ghs.assessment: The narrator also wipes away the small spill of tears. 'Copying that' has no source basis, while 'now overflowing' exaggerates the deliberately limited ちょっとあふれた.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I wipe away the few tears that have spilled over.'

highlights.text: Copying that, I go and wipe those tears now overflowing.

rows.en: I reached over and wiped away the tear that spilled.

ghs.assessment: The mock self-congratulation survives; me gentleman is simply ungrammatical.
ghs.remedy: Use grammatical mock-gentleman wording.

highlights.text: Wah, me gentleman.

ghs.assessment: In response to thanks, なに dismisses the matter: 'Don't mention it' or 'It's nothing.' 'For what' instead asks a question and changes the social move.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It's nothing.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "For what."

ghs.en: I pass my gaze on the corridor.
ghs.assessment: The scanning direction remains clear through unidiomatic wording.
ghs.remedy: Describe the look direction naturally.

highlights.text: I pass my gaze on the corridor.

ghs.assessment: Surprise at the cleaning remains. The defects are grammar and discourse marking.
ghs.remedy: Express the surprise in grammatical English.

highlights.text: Taichi: "So anyway, cleaning are you."

rows.jp: 「体動かしていた方が落ち着くかなって」
rows.en: “I thought moving around might calm me down.”

ghs.en: Miki: "When the body is moving there is relaxation, it's said."
ghs.assessment: Miki says she thought moving her body might help her settle down. The English turns this personal, tentative motive into a generic assertion that movement produces relaxation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I thought moving around might help me calm down.'

highlights.text: Miki: "When the body is moving there is relaxation, it's said."

rows.jp: 不可抗力により偶然スカートがめくれてしまう
rows.en: Through circumstances beyond my control, her skirt happens to flip up
